title: Differential pair + tail
description: The bare differential-pair transconductor sized by half-circuit: one input device at half the tail current, plus the tail source that reads the input $V_{GS}$ to place its own headroom. The load is left abstract — a spec conductance gds_load_est (its inverse is the load resistance $R_L$) — so this sheet sizes the input stage independently of whatever mirror, resistor, or cascode terminates the drains. Differential gain, GBW, slew, input noise, offset, and the input common-mode range are author math over the two children. The common-mode gain and CMRR are estimate-grade (the tail output conductance sets them); a real CMRR also depends on drain-load and layout mismatch, so trust the sim for sign-off.

params.name: gds_load_est
params.note: conductance loading each drain; R_L = 1/gds_load_est. Set from the terminating load (mirror gds, resistor, or cascode)

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: nominal input CM at which the operating point is evaluated

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: drain DC level; sets the input device vds

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current, noise, and the CM-low edge

params.name: gm_id_tail
params.note: tail inversion: higher V* costs CM-low headroom but tightens the current source

params.name: vgs_est_in
params.note: estimate of the input-pair vgs, used to place the input drain node; retune until input-bias-consistent is green

doc.title: Input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current. Its drain sits at V_out_dc; its source sits one vgs below the input CM.

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device carrying the full bias current; its saturation headroom sets the CM-low edge, and its output conductance sets the common-mode rejection.

params.name: vds_t
params.note: the tail node: one input vgs below the input CM

rows.name: Gm
rows.note: differential-pair transconductance is the half-circuit gm

rows.name: Av
rows.note: half-circuit gain into the device gds in parallel with the load conductance

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: input-pair thermal density; add the load's own contribution per the terminating device

rows.name: vos
rows.note: input-pair Pelgrom offset; the load pair adds in quadrature once its geometry is known

rows.name: Acm
rows.note: estimate: common-mode gain magnitude, set by the tail output conductance splitting between the two halves

rows.name: CMRR
rows.note: estimate: differential gain over common-mode gain; a real CMRR also depends on load and layout mismatch, so trust the sim

rows.name: cm_lo_edge
rows.note: lowest input CM that keeps the tail saturated

rows.name: cm_hi_edge
rows.note: highest input CM that keeps the input device saturated at the drain DC level

rules.note: the spec'd CM-low must sit above the tail-saturation edge
the spec'd CM-high must sit below the input-saturation edge
estimate: a longer tail L (lower tail gds) lifts CMRR; sim owns the real number
the input drain node placement uses vgs_est_in; retune it to the reported in__vgs if this trips
